pages.title: MC3DPrint Terminal
pages.text: An $(l)Applied Energistics 2$() cable part that lists what your printers and Fabricators can make, and orders it paid in $(l)Filament Units$().$(br2)It $(l)dispatches$(), it does not craft: an order costs what printing it by hand would.$(br2)Needs AE2 installed.

pages.title: Losing The Channel
pages.text: The terminal uses a $(l)channel$(), like AE2's own terminals, so a busy network wants a dense cable or a controller.$(br2)With no channel it goes $(l)offline$(): an open screen closes and nothing new is dispatched.$(br2)A running order $(l)holds$() until the network is back, and spends nothing while it waits.

pages.title: Connecting Machines
pages.text: A printer or Fabricator joins the network by $(l)touching$() it. Put the machine against any AE2 cable or device and the cable $(l)connects to it$(), the same as any AE2 machine.$(br2)It costs no channel. No MC3D Cable, interface or storage bus is involved.$(br2)On a Fabricator the $(l)controller$() must touch the network, not the casing.

pages.title: Why A Tier Greys
pages.text: A tier is orderable when your $(l)best machine's tier$() is at least that tier, however much filament you have.$(br2)So $(o)Needs a T6 machine; your best is T4$() means build or connect a bigger machine.$(br2)Distance never matters: a machine is either touching the network or it is not.

pages.title: What It Lists
pages.text: The terminal lists what your network is $(l)already holding$(), not every item in the game. It reprints what you own.$(br2)Stock decides what is $(l)listed$(). It never decides what can be $(l)ordered$(): a wind-only item or a restricted trophy stays greyed and refused even with a drive full of it plugged in.$(br2)Blacklisted means blacklisted, whether or not you own one.

pages.title: The Catalog
pages.text: Every stocked item that carries a price appears, sorted by tier then cost.$(br2)What you $(l)cannot$() order stays listed and greyed, with the reason, so it tells you what to go build.$(br2)Scroll with the wheel or drag the bar on the right. Search matches the name $(l)and$() the registry id.

pages.title: The Tier Rail
pages.text: One row per tier down the left, showing the filament that could pay a cost at that tier. Hover for exact numbers.$(br2)Each row counts its own tier $(l)and every tier above it$(), because spending is down-only: a Tier 3 spool pays a Tier 1 cost, a Tier 1 spool never pays a Tier 3 one.$(br2)A single combined total would be the number that lies to you.

pages.title: Orders
pages.text: Click an item to $(l)select$() it. Type a quantity, or use $(o)-$() and $(o)+$() (Shift steps by ten, 9999 max), then press $(l)Print$().$(br2)Click one of your own orders to $(l)cancel$() it. An order binds to one machine, so two never spend the same spools.$(br2)Filament is charged as each item is made, and given $(l)back$() to the tiers it came from if that item cannot be delivered.

pages.title: When It Holds
pages.text: Interruptions $(l)hold$() rather than fail: no filament, no power, or nowhere to put the output all pause and resume on their own.$(br2)If the machine leaves the network, or you claim it by hand, the order is handed $(l)back$() to the queue and finds somewhere else to run.$(br2)An unformed Fabricator is never offered one.

pages.title: Taking It Back
pages.text: Load a disc, or drop an item in a printer's template slot, and that machine is yours again at once.$(br2)Any terminal order it was running is handed back to the queue and finds somewhere else to run. A terminal order $(l)never$() interrupts work you started by hand.
An AE2 $(item)Crafting Terminal$() ringed by eight $(item)Extrudium Crystals$().
